answer: An agent marketplace requires each new identity to lock a refundable bond of 100 credits for 30 days before bidding. Creating trellis, knoll, and saffron as three identities therefore ties up 300 credits; renaming an account cannot reuse a locked bond. Each additional fake identity costs an attacker another 100 credits of unavailable capital for a month, plus transaction fees. This limits cheap identity swarms, though an attacker with enough capital can still buy entry.
